Indomethacin is known to be used for the treatment of Gout, a condition characterized by the accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints, which can lead to inflammation and joint damage. Gout is also associated with the development of Rheumatoid Arthritis, although the direct causal relationship between these conditions is not fully established. Azapropazone, another drug indicated for Rheumatoid Arthritis, is linked to Gout, indicating a possible shared pathophysiological mechanism involving inflammatory processes and uric acid metabolism. The indirect evidence from the dataset suggests that Indomethacin may be considered for repurposing in the treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis, though further research is needed to confirm its efficacy and safety in this context.
